privacyPolicy.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPolicy.description: A plain-language summary of how this site handles contact details, browser storage, analytics, and marketing tools.
privacyPolicy.reviewNotice: This page describes the current implementation in plain language. It is not legal advice and still needs review by a qualified privacy professional before it is treated as final policy text.

introduction.title: Introduction
introduction.content: This page explains what information the site handles when you browse, change privacy settings, or choose to get in touch. It avoids making a blanket compliance claim.

dataController.title: Data Controller
dataController.content: Eduard Sergiu Stefan operates this website and is the contact for the personal data described here. Use the email address in the Contact section for privacy questions or requests.

dataCollected.title: Data We Collect
dataCollected.intro: The site may handle the following information:

items.email: Contact details you choose to provide, such as your name and email address
items.message: Information you choose to share in a message or booking request
items.technicalInfo: Technical and usage information processed by hosting and analytics tools, which may include IP address, browser, device, pages viewed, and interactions

purpose.title: How the Information Is Used
purpose.intro: Information is used for these purposes:

items.communication: To reply when you choose to contact or schedule with Eduard
items.booking: To manage a booking or understand the context you share in a message
items.analytics: To understand site usage and improve the experience, with optional analytics and marketing controlled through the privacy settings

legalBasis.title: Choices and Legal Basis
legalBasis.content: Contact information is used to respond to a request you choose to make. PostHog stays in cookieless mode when optional tracking is declined; opted-in PostHog tracking and Meta Pixel run only after you accept them. The applicable legal bases and final wording must be confirmed during professional legal review.

dataRetention.title: Data Retention
dataRetention.content: This site does not currently publish a verified fixed retention period for every service. Contact records and vendor retention settings should be reviewed, documented, and added here before this policy is treated as final. You can ask for your information to be deleted.

yourRights.title: Your Rights
yourRights.intro: Depending on the law that applies, you may have rights such as:

items.access: Accessing the personal data held about you
items.erasure: Asking for your personal data to be deleted
items.restriction: Asking for limits on how your data is used
items.dataPortability: Receiving eligible data in a portable format
items.object: Objecting to certain uses of your personal data

yourRights.contact: To make a privacy request, email contact@eduardstefan.dev.

analytics.title: Browser Storage, Analytics, and Marketing
analytics.content: The site stores your privacy choice in local storage. PostHog is configured to use cookieless mode when optional tracking is declined. If you accept optional tracking, PostHog may use browser storage or cookies, and Meta Pixel may load to measure visits and contact actions. You can change this choice from Manage cookies in the footer. Other site features, such as theme or scheduling preferences, may also use browser storage or a session cookie.

dataSecurity.title: Data Security
dataSecurity.content: Information is handled through the site's hosting, analytics, scheduling, and communication services. Access should be limited to what is needed, but no online service can promise complete security. Vendor configuration and access controls still need to be checked as part of the legal review.

changes.title: Changes to This Policy
changes.content: This page may change when the site's forms, storage, analytics, marketing tools, or vendors change. The last-updated date will be revised with material edits.

contact.title: Contact
contact.content: For questions about this page, or to request access, correction, or deletion, email contact@eduardstefan.dev.

cookieBanner.description: This site stores your choice in this browser. Optional analytics and marketing run only with your permission. Read the

essential.title: Essential storage
essential.description: Keeps your privacy choice and basic site preferences. It cannot be switched off in this panel.

optional.description: Allows PostHog analytics and Meta Pixel to measure visits and contact actions. PostHog uses cookieless mode when this is off.

faq.label: FAQ
faq.headline: Questions you might have
faq.subtitle: The stuff teams usually ask before we start.

faq-1.question: How long does a project take?
faq-1.answer: A focused build can take a few weeks; a larger platform or migration can take several months. I give you a delivery plan after understanding the systems, dependencies, and decision-makers involved.

faq-2.question: What kinds of products do you build?
faq-2.answer: Marketing sites, content platforms, portals, dashboards, integrations, and the front-end systems connecting them. I focus on web surfaces used by established product and marketing teams.

faq-3.question: Will our team own the result?
faq-3.answer: Yes. The code lives in your repository, decisions are documented, and the handoff is part of the work. I can stay involved, but the system should never depend on me being there.

faq-4.question: Do you work with our existing designers and developers?
faq-4.answer: Yes. I'm comfortable plugging into an existing team, matching your conventions, and handing off cleanly. I can also run a project solo end to end if that's what you need.

faq-5.question: What technology do you use?
faq-5.answer: Usually React, Next.js, and TypeScript, integrated with the systems your team already uses. For structured content, Sanity is my specialty. The architecture follows the job rather than forcing every project into the same stack.

faq-6.question: Can you improve an existing platform instead of replacing it?
faq-6.answer: Yes. A rebuild is not automatically the right answer. I can work inside an existing codebase, improve the highest-cost areas first, and help your team decide what should be retained, refactored, or replaced.

fit.goodFitTitle: Sanity is likely a fit when
goodFit: Multiple teams publish across channels or regions
Content structure and reuse matter more than free-form pages
Your workflow needs previews, roles, or custom editorial tools
You want a front-end independent from the CMS
notFit: The site is small, static, and changes rarely
Editors only need a handful of fixed pages
Your team cannot own a custom front-end
The platform cost outweighs the workflow benefit

faq.label: FAQ
faq.headline: Questions teams ask before committing to Sanity
faq.subtitle: The practical answers—including the trade-offs.

items.question: Can you migrate us from WordPress or Contentful?
items.answer: Yes. I inventory the source content, map it into the new model, migrate assets and references, preserve URLs where possible, create redirects where needed, and validate the result before launch.

items.question: Will editors need developer help to publish pages?
items.answer: Routine publishing should not require it. The page system defines safe, reusable choices for editors while developers retain control over the components and constraints that protect the brand.

items.question: Are we locked into Sanity?
items.answer: Partly. Sanity is a vendor decision, and pretending otherwise would be misleading. Your front-end remains standard code in your repository, your schemas are code you own, and your content can be exported. Moving later still takes work, but it remains a real option.

items.question: Can you work with our existing designers and developers?
items.answer: Yes. I can own the Sanity and front-end work end to end or work inside an existing team, matching its design system, repository conventions, review process, and release workflow.

items.question: What happens after launch?
items.answer: Your team receives training, documentation, and ownership of the code and content model. I can hand over completely or continue as an embedded partner for new workflows, components, and integrations.
